newsitem.title: USA: Citicorp names ex-CIA head Deutch to board.
newsitem.headline: Citicorp names ex-CIA head Deutch to board.

text.p: Citicorp on Tuesday named John Deutch to its board of directors, less than a week after he resigned as director of the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency.

Deutch, 58, will make $40,000 a year as a Citicorp board member -- $10,000 of which he'll be paid in Citicorp stock -- as well as $950 per board meeting. He can expect to attend "at least" 20 meetings, a Citicorp spokesman said.

Deutch, who formally resigned as CIA Director on December 13, had indicated earlier this year he would leave the job. President Clinton on December 5 nominated national security advisor Anthony Lake to replace him.
Deutch had served as a director on Citicorp's board from 1987 to 1993, when he resigned to take the CIA job.
His appointnment brings Citicorp's board to 14 members, the company said.
